::: {.why}
Engle-Granger picks a left-hand side and a right-hand side, and the answer depends on which you picked, which is a defect Johansen does not have.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the difference between Engle-Granger and Johansen, and say which you would run given two price series and which given six.
- Show, on your own data, a pair where reversing the Engle-Granger regression changes the conclusion.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Find the asymmetry: run Engle-Granger both ways round on all pairs from your 50-name universe and count how many change their verdict at 5 percent when the regression is reversed. That count is the practical argument for Johansen.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Run Johansen on a three-asset system, such as three ETFs tracking related exposures, and interpret the trace statistic: how many cointegrating relations, and what the first eigenvector says about the hedge weights. Compare its implied weights against the Engle-Granger slope for the corresponding pair.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the decision rule into the milestone report: which procedure for two series, which for many, and the one-sentence reason.
:::
:::
